name: image-compare
description: Before/after image comparison with a draggable, keyboard-operable divider (role="slider"), labelled sides, hover-follow and vertical modes

after.description: The full picture underneath — the "after" side. Its alt should say so ("After: …")

before.description: The picture on top, clipped at the divider — the "before" side, on the inline-start (or top) side. Same dimensions as after

before-label.description: Visible chip naming the before side (aria-hidden: the alts and the slider's value text carry it)

after-label.description: Visible chip naming the after side (aria-hidden)

handle.description: The divider: role="slider", tabindex="0", aria-label, aria-valuemin 0 / max 100; aria-valuenow is the percentage of the width (or height) that shows the before picture, and aria-valuetext reads "60% before, 40% after"

grip.description: The round handle on the divider line, holding an aria-hidden arrows <svg>

orientation.description: horizontal: before on the inline-start side of a vertical divider. vertical: before on top of a horizontal divider. The controller mirrors it into aria-orientation

mode.description: drag: press and drag anywhere on the picture. hover: the divider also follows a mouse or pen without a press

position.description: Initial divider position, 0–100 (otherwise the handle's aria-valuenow). Also author style="--image-compare-pos: 50%" so the static page splits

step.description: Arrow-key step in percent; PageUp/PageDown move ten steps

dragging.description: A pointer is dragging the divider

methods.name: setPosition
methods.description: Move the divider to `percent` (0–100) of the way across.

required_attrs: alt on before and after naming each side

keyboard.ArrowRight / ArrowUp: move the divider one step toward the end (show more before); in RTL ArrowLeft
keyboard.ArrowLeft / ArrowDown: one step back; in RTL ArrowRight

notes: The handle is the only focusable element; a press anywhere on the picture moves it there and focuses it.
touch-action leaves the cross axis to the page, so a horizontal compare never traps a vertical scroll.
In RTL the before picture sits on the right, and the arrow keys follow the direction the divider moves.
